1. **^** Presidents are numbered according to uninterrupted periods served by the same person. For example, George Washington served two consecutive terms and is counted as the first president (not the first and second). Grover Cleveland was both the 22nd president and the 24th president because his two terms were not consecutive. A vice president who temporarily becomes acting president under the Twenty-fifth Amendment to the Constitution is not counted, because the president remains in office during such a period.

<document>
<title>List of presidents of the United States by time in office</title>
<fragment>

Of the individuals elected president of the United States, four died of natural causes while in office (William Henry Harrison,[1] Zachary Taylor,[2] Warren G. Harding[3] and Franklin D. Roosevelt), four were assassinated (Abraham Lincoln,[4] James A. Garfield,[4][5] William McKinley[6] and John F. Kennedy) and one resigned from office (Richard Nixon).[7]


William Henry Harrison spent the shortest time in office, while Franklin D. Roosevelt spent the longest. Roosevelt is the only American president to have served more than two terms. Following ratification of the Twenty-second Amendment in 1951, presidents—beginning with Dwight D. Eisenhower—have been ineligible for election to a third term or, after serving more than two years of a term to which some other person was elected president, to a second term. The amendment contained a grandfather clause that explicitly exempted the incumbent president, then Harry S. Truman, from the new term limitations.

chat_history.content:
Based on the historical information I've gathered, here are the U.S. presidents who belonged to the Democratic-Republican Party:

## Democratic-Republican Presidents

1. **Thomas Jefferson** (1801-1809)
   - Co-founder of the Democratic-Republican Party with James Madison
   - 3rd President of the United States

2. **James Madison** (1809-1817)
   - Co-founder of the Democratic-Republican Party
   - 4th President of the United States
   - Served as Secretary of State under Jefferson before becoming president

3. **James Monroe** (1817-1825)
   - 5th President of the United States
   - His presidency was known as the "Era of Good Feelings" when the Democratic-Republican Party was essentially the only major political party

## About the Party

The Democratic-Republican Party existed from **1792 to 1834** and was one of the two major parties during America's First Party System. The party was founded by Thomas Jefferson and James Madison with the ideology of:

- Jeffersonian democracy
- Agrarianism
- Liberalism
- Anti-clericalism
- Republicanism

The party eventually dissolved in the 1820s-1830s, with its members splitting into what became the modern Democratic Party (led by Andrew Jackson) and the National Republican Party (which later evolved into the Whig Party and eventually the modern Republican Party).

It's sometimes referred to as the "Jeffersonian Republicans" or simply the "Republican Party" during its time, but it's distinct from today's Republican Party.
